ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The outside of the figure is a large square, divided into four parts by a vertical line and a horizontal line: the lower left is a square labeled 81 cm^2, the upper left is a rectangle labeled 18 cm^2, the lower right is a rectangle labeled vertically with 18 cm^2, and the upper right is a small square; the arrow and question mark on the right indicate that the side length of the large square is to be found. Reasoning: The lower-left region is a square and has an area of 81 cm^2, so its side length is sqrt(81)=9 cm. The upper-left rectangle shares the same width with this 81 cm^2 square, namely 9 cm; its area is 18 cm^2, so its height is 18/9=2 cm. This 2 cm is the height added above the 9 cm square, therefore the side length of the large square is 9+2=11 cm.
